text: The evidence, judged . read it (19 min) · the slides (talk at Perplexity, 3 November 2026) · logs and code (KeAWang/associative-memory-blog) · discussion (670 points, 152 comments on 27 November 2026) The idea in one sentence: a linear layer, an MLP and softmax attention all recall a stored value by weighting every stored value by its key's similarity to the query, so the leftover weight on all the wrong memories (interference) grows like √M; each step from the matrix to the MLP to attention shrinks the weight on keys that are only slightly similar, which lets one readout hold about d, then about d², then about e 2√d random memories before the interference is as large as the value it recalls.
